reason: Narrative summary of the leaders' dedication gifts, fulfilling C0830; 'the day he anointed it' is narration, not a direction.
Genealogy: 'summoned members of the congregation' is an epithet for Dathan and Abiram; no direction is stated.
Joshua's summons of the twelve tribal men opens the charge recorded at 4:5 ('summoned... and said to them'); same speaker and occasion.
Joshua's recital of the Lord's past deeds against the Amorites: historical narrative and doctrine that directs no one.
Recital of the Jericho conquest within Joshua's covenant speech: narrative, no direction.
Narrator's account of the Lord handing Israel to plunderers: narrative judgment, not a direction.

title: Shechem's men and Maallon's house make Abimelech king at Shechem
speaker: all the men of Shechem and the house of Maallon (Millo)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

Jephthah's self-defence and rhetorical question to Ephraim; it recounts the Lord's deliverance and directs no one.
Narrative of Samuel's mourning and the Lord's regret over making Saul king; no direction.
Fulfilment narrative: Samuel carries out ot-1-samuel-v16-12 ('Rise and anoint David') without quoting or expressly citing the command.
David's rebuke of Abner with a rhetorical challenge ('where are the spear and flask?'): a verdict, not a direction to act.
Narrative: the foreigners hear that David was anointed and march out; no direction.
Narrative of David ending his fast; the narrated request for bread is ordinary speech, not recorded.

context: Jonathan reports to Adonijah that David made Solomon king: anointed by Zadok and Nathan at Gihon, now seated on the throne.
reason: Jonathan's report retells David's appointment (1:34–35) in its own terms; 1:43–46 are one report unit, not plain fulfilment narrative.
Inventory of the bronze work Hiram made for Solomon: narrative, no direction.

context: The elders do as written in Jezebel's letters: they proclaim the fast, seat Naboth at the head, and the false witnesses testify.
reason: Fulfilment that expressly cites the letters ('did as Jezebel had sent... as written in the documents') and repeats their wording; link 20:11–13.
Narrative of Edom's revolt; the installation of an unnamed king is incidental and states no commission or direction.

Narrative: the foreigners hear that David was anointed and march out; no direction.
David's summons names the priests and Levite chiefs addressed in 15:12 ('He said to them'); same speaker, occasion and charge.
Garbled genealogical aside in the gatekeeper list: the appointee is unnamed and unclear; no stated direction or commission.
Battle narrative: the Lord hands Israel over to Judah; no direction.
Narrative epithet 'the Lord's anointed—Ahab's house' mentions Jehu's commission (AUD-12-9-6) without restating it; the charge is implied, not stated.

title: The people of the land make sixteen-year-old Uzziah king
speaker: all the people of the land
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated popular king-making, as published AUD-10-2-4; same accession as held GAP-12-14-21 (2 Kings 14:21): publish one record citing both.
Narrative of the Lord delivering Ahaz to the kings of Syria and Israel; no direction.

title: The people of the land anoint Jehoahaz and make him king
speaker: the people of the land
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated anointing and installation, like published AUD-10-2-4; same event as held GAP-12-23-30 (2 Kings 23:30): publish one record citing both.
Salutation of the second letter (senders, recipients, greeting); the letter's directions are recorded at 2 Maccabees 1:18 and 2:16.

title: Antiochus summons Menelaus and Sostratus over the unpaid royal funds
speaker: King Antiochus (Epiphanes)
recipient: Menelaus the high priest and Sostratus, commander of the citadel

Judas's same exhortation continues: he gives orders, exposes the nations' perjury and arms his men with encouraging words.

Psalm confession that the Lord saved His anointed: praise and doctrine, not a direction.
Psalm title ('before being anointed') and a declaration of trust; no direction addressed to anyone.
Lament addressed to God about rejecting His anointed: prayer, out of scope.
Historical recital of God handing Israel over to the nations: narrative, no direction.
Divine promise of a horn and a lamp for David's anointed: a promise that directs no one.

context: Ben Sira recalls the anointed priest's grain offering: wholly offered twice every day, continually (Leviticus 6:13–15).
reason: Recalls C0434 point by point (continual, morning and evening halves, fully performed), as Sirach 45 is linked verse by verse elsewhere.

context: Ben Sira recalls God choosing Aaron from all the living to present offerings, incense and atonement for the people.
reason: 45:15 is already linked to C0298; 45:16 recalls Aaron's election to priestly service, matching C0285 (Exodus 28:1), which already links 45:6–7.

context: The Lord renews the charge in a later stanza: recognize that those you dreaded are mortal, withering like grass.
reason: Same directive not to fear mortal opponents, in a separate stanza of the oracle; linked as Additional Scripture, as K083 links Matthew 24:42–44.

context: An earlier oracle voices the same call: clear the roads and remove obstacles from My people's road.
reason: Quoted call repeating 62:10's direction (make a road for My people, clear its stones) more exactly than 40:3.

context: The Lord recalls the rule against taking back a divorced wife after another marriage, as an image of Israel's unfaithfulness.
reason: Expressly recalls the Deuteronomy 24:1–4 rule (divorce, remarriage, no return, pollution) and applies it figuratively.

context: Jeremiah tells Hananiah and the people to hear: a prophet of peace is known as truly sent when his word comes.
reason: Jeremiah restates the Deuteronomy 18:21–22 fulfilment test against Hananiah; 35:7 is the call to hear that introduces it.
Background recollection of Nebuchadnezzar making Zedekiah king; no current record. If held GAP-14-36-10 (2 Chronicles 36:10) is recorded, link this there.

context: Earlier in the same call the Lord sends Ezekiel to speak His words to the house of Israel, warning they will not listen.
reason: Same commission ('go, enter... speak My words') in a separate speech of the call narrative; Additional Scripture rather than a split primary range.

context: Ezekiel's temple law restates the rule: no priest drinks wine when entering the inner court.
reason: Repeats Leviticus 10:9; within Ezekiel the verse sits only in the broad ot-ezekiel-v44-13 range, so linking adds the restatement.

context: Matthew's form of the salt saying: disciples are the earth's salt; salt that loses its taste is thrown out.
reason: Same saying about salt losing its saltiness as Mark 9:50; K045 (Matthew 5:14–16) carries a different image and direction.

context: Matthew sets Luke 13:28–29's warning after the centurion's faith: many from east and west recline; the kingdom's sons are cast out.
reason: 8:11–12 repeat the Luke 13:28–29 warning within AUD-46-13-22; 8:10 is Jesus' praise of the centurion, not part of it.

context: Matthew's account of the same raising: Jesus tells the mourners to withdraw, says the girl sleeps, and raises her.
reason: Same scene and order ('Withdraw') as Luke 8:52–54 and the linked Mark 5:39–41.

context: Matthew gives Mark 13:12 word for word, brother handing brother over to death; widens the linked 10:22 to 10:21–22.
reason: Verbatim repetition of Mark 13:12 directly before the already linked Matthew 10:22.

context: Jesus' testimony continues: none greater than John (Luke 7:28); the Law and Prophets until John; he is Elijah who is to come.
reason: Same speech as the linked Matthew 11:7–10; 11:11 matches Luke 7:28 and 11:14 names John the promised Elijah.

context: Jesus paraphrases Isaiah 6:9 before quoting it: seeing they do not see, hearing they do not hear or understand.
reason: 13:14–15 are already linked; 13:13 paraphrases the same Isaiah 6:9 message, as the linked Mark 4:12 does.

context: After the failed exorcism Jesus teaches that faith like a mustard seed will move a mountain, as in Mark 11:23.
reason: Same mountain-moving faith saying as Mark 11:23; AUD-44-17-14 (17:14–18) records a different order on that occasion.

context: Matthew's cleansing: Jesus drives out the traders and cites 'My house will be called a house of prayer' against the robbers' cave.
reason: Synoptic cleansing whose saying matches K023 (Mark 11:17); Luke 19:45–46 is linked there, not to John's AUD-47-2-13.
Already linked: 22:24, the quoted levirate rule, is on S156; 22:23, 25–28 are the Sadducees' setting and hypothetical, not a restatement.

context: Matthew's frame for the quoted Psalm: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is and how David can call Him Lord.
reason: 22:43–44 are already linked; adding the frame matches the linked Mark 12:35–37 and Luke 20:41–44, and 22:45 expressly recalls the quotation.

context: Matthew's discourse form: hated by all nations for Jesus' name, betrayal, false prophets, and the one who endures to the end saved.
reason: Matthew's parallel to Mark 13:12–13 (hatred for the name, handing over, endurance to the end); 24:11–12 describe the trials to be endured.

context: No one knows the day or hour; as in Noah's days, one is taken and one left, leading into 24:42's 'keep watch'.
reason: States the record's premise (the time is unknown) and its illustration, joining the linked Matthew 24:42–44.

context: Matthew's Bethany anointing: Jesus defends the woman, who prepared Him for burial; her deed will be told wherever the gospel is proclaimed.
reason: Link Jesus' defence (26:10–13), matching the linked Mark 14:6–9; 26:6–9 are the setting and the disciples' objection.

context: Jesus quotes Zechariah 13:7, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered,' of the disciples' desertion.
reason: 26:31 quotes Zechariah 13:7; 26:32 is Jesus' promise to go ahead to Galilee, not part of the quotation.
Passion narrative: the council binds Jesus and hands Him over to Pilate; no direction stated.

context: Matthew cites the thirty-silver oracle, attributed to Jeremiah, as fulfilled in the potter's field purchase, 'as the Lord directed me'.
reason: Fulfilment citation that quotes the Zechariah 11:13 direction (thirty silver pieces, the potter) and expressly invokes the Lord's directing.

context: Matthew's form of the demand: persuaded by the chief priests, the crowds choose Barabbas and cry 'Let Him be crucified!'; no law cited.
reason: Same demand for Jesus' crucifixion before Pilate as John 19:6; Matthew lacks the appeal to their law, so a link, not a record.

context: John's own proclamation of the stronger One coming after him, which Paul summarizes in Acts 19:4.
reason: Source of the instruction Paul recalls, linked as Malachi 3:1 is to AUD-46-7-24; no record holds John's proclamation itself.

context: That evening at Capernaum Jesus heals many and will not let the demons speak, because they knew Him.
reason: Silencing demons who know Him repeats AUD-46-4-35 (same Capernaum day, Mark 1:23–28 linked) more exactly than the charge to the healed.

context: Mark's account of the same reply to the critics: the sick need a physician; He came to call sinners.
reason: Same exchange as K021 (Matthew 9:11–13), without the Hosea citation; 2:15 is the meal setting, as Matthew 9:10 is outside K021.

context: Mark's form of the Matthew 12:15–16 summary: crowds healed, and He sternly warns the spirits not to make Him known.
reason: Same summary with the identical warning (Mark 3:12 = Matthew 12:16); 3:9 is already its own record (AUD-45-3-9).

context: Mark continues the leaven warning with the rebuke for not understanding, recalling the loaves, as Matthew 16:8–11.
reason: 8:14–16 are already linked; 8:17–21 parallel Matthew 16:8–11 inside K086's own passage.
Same Markan pericope as K023 (11:17): the expulsion and the ban on carrying vessels that the house-of-prayer saying explains; Luke 19:45–46 is linked there.
Already linked: 12:19, the quoted levirate rule, is on S156; 12:18, 20–23 are the Sadducees' setting and hypothetical, not a restatement.

context: No one knows the day or hour except the Father: the premise of 13:33's 'stay awake, for you do not know'.
reason: States the record's premise directly before the linked Mark 13:33–37; widens that link to 13:32–37.
